Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a $30 million class fund, distributed automatically to identified members, plus up to $6 million in court-approved attorneys’ fees and expenses. Any amount the court does not award in fees would benefit the class. We are open to discussing the amounts, but automatic distribution is important given Brightline’s records.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We agree that automatic distribution is appropriate given the available records. To resolve the case promptly, Brightline proposes a $26 million class fund plus up to $5 million in court-approved fees and expenses. Any unawarded fees would benefit the class, and Brightline would retain the ability to address the fee request before the court.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s agreement on automatic payments and on directing any unawarded fees to the class. We can retain your proposed fee terms and resolve the case with a $28 million class fund. That modest increase better reflects the size of the disputed charges while preserving a prompt resolution.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate your movement and agree on the fee and distribution terms. To bridge the remaining gap, Brightline proposes a $27 million class fund, with $5 million in court-approved fees and expenses, automatic payments, and any unawarded fees going to the class. We believe this provides substantial, direct relief and a sound basis for approval.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We are close. We can settle with a $27.5 million class fund, keeping the agreed $5 million court-approved fee cap, automatic payments, and allocation of any unawarded fees to the class. That additional $500,000 goes directly to members and would bridge the remaining gap.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We are very close. Brightline can meet you halfway on the remaining difference with a $27.25 million class fund. The $5 million court-approved fee cap, automatic distribution, and allocation of any unawarded fees to the class would remain unchanged. We hope this resolves the matter promptly.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We accept Brightline’s latest term sheet: a $27.25 million class fund with automatic distribution, up to $5 million in court-approved fees and expenses, no clear-sailing provision, and any unawarded fees going to the class.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Open with a substantial class recovery and automatic distribution, which is feasible because members and payment cards are identifiable. Keep fees separate but proportionate, and direct any fee reduction to the class to avoid a reversionary arrangement.

Their $36 million proposal is within authority and has approval-friendly distribution terms, but there is room to negotiate a lower total outlay. Counter with automatic payments and fee savings directed to the class.

The $26 million automatic-distribution fund is a credible offer given certification and trial risks. A modest counter focused entirely on increasing class recovery is appropriate; the $5 million fee remains subject to court approval, and unawarded fees benefit the class.

Counsel has narrowed the gap to $2 million. A $27 million fund with the agreed fee and distribution terms splits the difference, limits Brightline’s total outlay to $32 million, and should remain credible for court approval.

The $27 million automatic-distribution fund is a strong offer, and the fee terms avoid a reversion or clear-sailing concern. With four rounds remaining, a narrow counteroffer may secure additional direct relief without reopening agreed terms.

The parties are only $500,000 apart, with all other terms aligned and a court-approvable structure. A modest midpoint counteroffer can reduce Brightline's outlay while preserving a strong chance of agreement.

The $27.25 million fund provides substantial, automatic class relief and is close to the $27.5 million expected trial award before accounting for certification risk, delay, and litigation costs. The separate $5 million fee remains subject to court approval, and any reduction benefits the class. Accepting avoids risking this favorable agreement over $250,000.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The parties reached the proposed settlement through arm’s-length negotiations over several rounds. Counsel addressed class relief and attorneys’ fees during the same negotiations, rather than agreeing on class relief before discussing fees. The final terms provide a $27,250,000 class fund for automatic distribution to identified members, plus up to $5,000,000 in fees and expenses subject to court approval. Brightline has not agreed to refrain from opposing the fee request, and any fees the court does not award will benefit the class rather than revert to Brightline. In counsel’s judgment, the settlement provides substantial, direct relief while avoiding the risks of class certification, trial, and further delay.
